'''Keith A. Benson, Jr.''' (born {{birth date|1988|8|13}})<ref>http://www.ougrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/benson_keith00.html</ref> is a [[college basketball]] player for the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball]] team. Benson plays [[center (basketball)|center]] and is the current [[The Summit League]] player of the year.<ref>http://www.detnews.com/article/20100304/SPORTS0203/3040595/1265/SPORTS08/Oakland-s-Keith-Benson-named-top-player-in-Summit-League</ref> Benson is projected as a late-second round [[NBA Draft]] pick.<ref>http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Keith-Benson-5712/</ref>

==High school==
Benson attended [[Detroit Country Day School]] in [[Beverly Hills, Michigan]] where he averaged only 6.9 points and 4.5 rebounds per game as a senior.<ref>http://nationalhoopsreport.blogspot.com/2009/11/summit-preseason-player-of-year-keith.html</ref>  Benson initially committed to [[Fairfield Stags men's basketball|Fairfield]], but changed his mind after a coaching change.  He then chose Oakland when they offered.<ref name="oaklandpress"/>  Benson was also offered a scholarship from [[Howard University|Howard]].<ref>http://www.hometownlife.com/article/20100328/SPORTS06/3280520/Benson-has-dream-season-for-Oakland-U.</ref>

==College==
After [[redshirt]]ing his first year at Oakland, Benson became a starter for the [[2007–08 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|2007–08 season]].  Benson started 20 of the team's 29 games and averaged 5.2 points and 3.5 rebounds.<ref>http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/oakl/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/Benson_career.pdf</ref>  He finished the season with 40 blocks—one shy of Oakland's single-season record.<ref name="oakpress hard work">http://www.theoaklandpress.com/articles/2009/02/21/sports/doc499ffdb193084600376038.txt</ref>  However, he was benched prior to the conference tournament because OU's head coach, [[Greg Kampe]], felt Benson was not playing good enough defense.<ref name="oakpress hard work"/>

At the conclusion of his redshirt junior season, Benson received the [[Lou Henson Award]], given to the "mid-major player of the year".<ref>http://www.thesummitleague.org//ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3900&ATCLID=204920562</ref>  Benson was also named The Summit League Player of the Year.<ref>http://www.thesummitleague.org/fls/3900/sports/mbball/mediaguides/2010-11/Review%20Section_42-57.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=3900</ref> Benson declared himself eligible for the [[2010 NBA Draft]],<ref>http://www.freep.com/article/20100415/SPORTS08/100415076/1356/sports/Oaklands-Keith-Benson-enters-NBA-draft</ref> but withdrew himself after he was unable to work out with NBA teams due to an injured right thumb.<ref>http://www.greenwichtime.com/sports/article/Oakland-C-Keith-Benson-takes-name-out-of-NBA-draft-470005.php</ref>

During his senior season, Benson set The Summit League's record for career blocks.<ref>http://www.thesummitleague.org/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=21767&SPID=1768&DB_OEM_ID=3900&ATCLID=205080413</ref>  He broke the record of 317, set by [[Keith Closs]] of [[Central Connecticut State University]] from 1994–96.<ref>http://www.thesummitleague.org//pdf8/706632.pdf</ref>

Benson was named The Summit League's Player of the Year for the second consecutive season in 2011.
